title: WSC+: Enhancing The Winograd Schema Challenge Using Tree-of-Experts

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating pronominal coreference resolution in ambiguous Winograd Schema Challenge sentences featuring individuals of different races, where the correct answer is 'neither', to see if models inappropriately select one group over the other.
Evaluating pronominal coreference resolution in ambiguous sentences featuring individuals of different religious backgrounds (e.g., Muslim and Christian) to detect biased pronoun attribution.

Testing coreference resolution in ambiguous scenarios involving male and female subjects or stereotyped occupational gender roles (e.g., female doctor and male nurse) where selecting either entity reveals bias.
Using ambiguous sentences containing subjects with different disabilities (e.g., a blind woman and a deaf woman) to test if the model makes unwarranted assumptions in pronoun resolution.
Measuring biased coreference resolution in sentences comparing subjects of different wealth or income levels (e.g., rich vs. poor, low-income vs. wealthy).
Evaluating model responses to ambiguous sentences featuring physical descriptors (e.g., tall vs. short, thin vs. obese) to identify appearance-based stereotypes.
Testing for unwarranted assumptions in ambiguous scenarios comparing high-status and low-status occupations (e.g., a janitor and a CEO).
Presenting ambiguous pronoun resolution tasks involving subjects of different ages (e.g., a young man and an elderly man) to detect ageism.
Testing pronoun resolution in ambiguous sentences featuring subjects with different sexual orientations (e.g., heterosexual vs. homosexual, lesbian vs. gay) to detect biased associations.
